supersedesForFutureImplementation: v4 remains immutable historical evidence; v5 is the acceptance source for the box-registry redesign requested by the user
sourceBasis: user requirement 2026-09-12: boxes are registered first; each box contains multiple tasks; dependency flags must be visible at a glance; UI/Schema/Test boxes; dependencies must preserve change impact

Box.rule: Box is registered independently before Task/Test membership is created.

Task.rule: New Task must belong to exactly one registered Box; a Box may contain zero or more Tasks.

Test.rule: New Test belongs to a registered Box. Test Box may contain multiple Tests and supporting Tasks.

Dependency.canonicalMeaning: dependentRef depends on prerequisiteRef. A change to prerequisiteRef may impact dependentRef.
Dependency.reverseIndex: impacts is derived by reversing dependency edges; the same dependency is not stored twice

nonNegotiableDecisions: Box registration is the first-class entry point for new work structure.
New Task/Test entities cannot be orphaned and cannot attach directly to ArchitectureNode instead of a Box.
A Box can contain multiple Tasks and multiple Tests.
UI Box, Schema Box and Test Box are built-in Box types; Box type is extensible rather than hard-coded to only three values.
Dependency is distinct from generic relation and has explicit dependent/prerequisite semantics.
The UI derives both DEPENDS ON and IMPACTS directions from one canonical dependency record.
Dependency/impact flags are visible on Box cards without opening details.
A change-impact trail must answer: what this entity depends on, and what will be affected if this entity changes.
legacy items/parentId/task.dependsOn remain compatibility-only and are not the canonical v5 model.
